title: Etale–pro-etale cohomology comparison for arbitrary abelian sheaves
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison geometric morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] of its small sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and every integer $i\geq0$, the canonical cohomology pullback is an isomorphism of abelian groups $$H^i(T_{\mathrm{et}},F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(T_{\mathrm{proet}},
u_T^{-1}F).$$ Here cohomology means right derived global sections and $
u_T^{-1}$ is the abelian-sheaf inverse image [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. There is no torsion, finiteness, constructibility, or fixed coefficient ring assumption.

proof.text: Work with A = AddCommGrpCat in universe u+1 and L = comparisonUpperStar A T, R = comparisonLowerStar A T. These are the canonical abelian comparison functors. The existing instances make L additive and exact and R additive and left exact; the sheaf categories are Grothendieck abelian, hence have enough injectives. Use the existing generic Grothendieck-abelian coefficient comparison-unit theorem, specialized to A, to obtain an invertible unit on every sheaf, in particular on injectives.

proof.text: The existing arbitrary-coefficient injective acyclicity theorem says R.rightAcyclic (L.obj I) for every injective etale abelian sheaf I. Apply the generic derived-unit criterion to the unit from step 1 and this acyclicity. Its component is invertible at every bounded-below derived object. Mathlib Adjunction.fullyFaithfulLOfIsIsoUnit therefore makes L.mapDerivedCategoryPlus fully faithful.

For any sheaves X,Y and n at least zero, take their degree-zero single objects, with the target shifted by n. Both objects belong to D+: the shifted target has lower bound -n. The inclusion D+ to D is fully faithful, so the Hom map of L.mapDerivedCategory between these objects is bijective. Conjugate this Hom bijection by the canonical single-functor isomorphisms and the shift comparison. Ext.homEquiv identifies the resulting map with L.mapExtAddHom X Y n, exactly by Ext.mapExactFunctor_hom. This is the completely proved private helper mapExt_bijective_of_derivedPlus_fullyFaithful, and uses no injective-preservation assertion for L.

source.place: Private Ext/Hom bridge; Mathlib Ext.mapExactFunctor_hom and Iso.homCongr

proof.text: By its unchanged definition comparisonCohomologyMap is L.mapExtAddHom from the constant integral sheaf followed by Ext.precompAddEquiv for the canonical constant-sheaf comparison. The former is bijective by step 3 and the latter is an additive equivalence. Their composite is therefore bijective in every nonnegative degree, including degree zero. This proves the specified canonical map without choosing an unrelated Leray isomorphism.
